newsitem.title: USA: America Online Q1 revenues rise 77 percent.
newsitem.headline: America Online Q1 revenues rise 77 percent.

text.p: America Online Inc said Thursday that its first quarter revenue increased 77 percent to $349.9 million from $197.9 million a year ago, driven by growth in its subscriber base and higher revenues from advertising and electronic commerce.

America Online reported a first quarter net loss of $353.7 million, or $3.80 a share, as expected, due to a write off of $385.2 million for deferred subscriber acquisition costs. The company announced its write-off plans last week.
A year ago, America Online had a net loss of $10.9 million, or $0.14 a share, including a charge.

America Online said that its other revenues rose to a record of $38.8 million, roughly 24 percent above the June quarter levels. AOL said that eight advertisers have committed to spending $1 million or more this fiscal year, as it moves to seek more revenues beyond its base subscriber fees.

AOL its customer retention rate improved as the quarter progressed, reaching its best levels in September since mid-1995. AOL also said it saw strong subscriber growth following its September launch of its new marketing campaigns. It added 400,000 new subscribers in the first fiscal quarter.

With the addition of nearly 275,000 new members in the month of October, (its first fiscal quarter ended September 30), AOL said its total subscriber count reached 6.9 million worldwide. AOL also said average hourly usage improved to 6.95 hours per member in the recent period, and in October, hit its highest level in the company's history.

"In the spring we indicated that member growth would slow in the summer, but would likely pick back up in the fall as we rolled out our 3.0 software and increased our marketing expenditures," said AOL Chairman Steve Case. "We're please to report that growth has indeed accelerated, and, now....we believe we are poised for continued strong growth."

Last week, AOL said it would write-off $385 million in the September quarter to account for the balance of its hefty subscriber acquisition costs, such as its mass mailing of floppy disks. It had been deferring certain marketing costs and amortizing some costs over a period of 24 months.
AOL also said that due to its flat-rate pricing option that it announced last week, it expects lower margins, but that it lacks historical experience with this pricing model.

Before the charge, AOL reported first quarter net earnings of $19 million, or a profit of $0.17 a share. A year ago, AOL reported net income, excluding a charge for acquired research and development, of $6.1 million, or $0.06 a share.
According to First Call, the consensus on Wall Street was for AOL to report a profit of $0.17 a share, before any charges. The range on Wall Street was from $0.16 to $0.19.
